territory: CNS therapy platform — eShunt as platform for CNS therapy delivery/diagnostics beyond CSF drainage
doctrine_note: Per #7 M10 lesson — physics pre-check executed BEFORE elaborate prior-art searches. Preserves ALL physics pre-check results including killed premises. Push-the-envelope doctrine: every failure creates a search for a better mechanism. The machine kills its own inventions; honest negatives documented.

mechanisms.name: Sustained-release drug depot integrated into eShunt wall (antibiotics, anti-inflammatories, anti-proliferatives)
AAV gene therapy delivery via eShunt lumen (acute bolus for CNS genetic diseases)
Cell therapy delivery (stem cells, neural progenitors) via eShunt lumen
CSF sampling/diagnostic port (chronic CSF access for biomarker monitoring)
Neuromodulation electrode integrated into eShunt (DBS via venous access)
CAR-T / immunotherapy delivery for CNS tumors (leptomeningeal metastases)
Anti-amyloid antibody delivery (aducanumab, lecanemab via CSF)
Chemotherapy delivery for leptomeningeal metastases via eShunt
Continuous ICP monitoring as standalone diagnostic (separate from drainage)
CSF biosensor integration (glucose, lactate, beta-amyloid, tau, NfL, inflammatory markers)

step_1_brainstorm_summary.core_tension_identified: FUNDAMENTAL TENSION: eShunt's primary function is to DRAIN CSF (with dissolved therapeutics) to the venous system. Any CHRONIC drug depot that releases therapeutic INTO the CSF lumen will have that therapeutic rapidly drained away (~0.35 mL/min CSF production = ~5 min half-life for CSF drug clearance in eShunt patient). This is a UNIQUE physics constraint of the eShunt platform compared to VP shunts (which drain to peritoneum where drug clearance is ~30 min half-life). This tension does NOT affect ACUTE bolus delivery (drainage can be paused 1-4h post-injection) or SENSORS (sensor reads CSF; drainage removes sampled CSF but sensor stays).

M1_drug_depot_in_eshunt_wall.core_mechanism: Polymer matrix containing antibiotic/anti-inflammatory embedded in eShunt wall, releasing drug into surrounding tissue (sinus wall) or CSF over weeks-months.
M1_drug_depot_in_eshunt_wall.problem_addressed: Prophylactic antibiotic to prevent shunt infection (1-5% rate, devastating); anti-inflammatory to prevent fibrosis/foreign-body reaction at venous interface.
M1_drug_depot_in_eshunt_wall.plausible_physical_principle: Drug elution from polymer matrix well-established (drug-eluting stents since 2003 — Cypher, Taxus). Higuchi model: dM/dt = (D*A*C_s)/(2L). Rifampin-clindamycin-impregnated VP shunts (Bactiseal) standard-of-care since 2003.
M1_drug_depot_in_eshunt_wall.magnitude_estimate: Antibiotic prophylaxis reduces shunt infection from 5% to 2% (50% relative reduction). Drug release kinetics: 7-14 days burst, 4-8 weeks sustained.
M1_drug_depot_in_eshunt_wall.physiology_verdict: PARTIAL_CONCERN — drug elution INTO CSF lumen is rapidly cleared by eShunt drainage (half-life ~5 min vs ~30 min for VP shunt draining to peritoneum). Drug elution INTO sinus wall tissue (not CSF) is unaffected by drainage.
known_constraints: eShunt CSF drainage rate 0.35 mL/min = 500 mL/day; CSF turnover ~3x daily (vs ~3x DAILY in VP patient with peritoneal absorption)
Drug released INTO CSF has clearance half-life ~5 min (eShunt) vs ~30 min (VP shunt) — 6x faster clearance
Drug released INTO sinus wall tissue (sub-endothelial) is unaffected — sinus wall is destination tissue, not CSF
M1_drug_depot_in_eshunt_wall.novelty_concern_pre_check: HIGHLY SATURATED for prophylactic antibiotic — Bactiseal (Codman), ARES (Medtronic) impregnated VP shunts are standard-of-care. eShunt-specific antibiotic elution is a routine adaptation, not patentable.
M1_drug_depot_in_eshunt_wall.advance_verdict: SATURATED_FOR_ANTIBIOTIC / PARTIAL_CONCERN_FOR_CHRONIC_DELIVERY — antibiotic prophylaxis saturated; chronic therapeutic drug delivery is compromised by rapid CSF clearance. WEAK_NOVEL.
M1_drug_depot_in_eshunt_wall.honest_negative_finding: The eShunt's primary DRAINAGE function fundamentally conflicts with chronic drug delivery into CSF lumen. Drug elution into surrounding sinus wall tissue (anti-proliferative to prevent intimal hyperplasia, anti-inflammatory for FBR) is feasible but is closer to TERRITORY #7 (venous interface protection) than TERRITORY #9 (CNS therapy platform).

M2_aav_gene_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.core_mechanism: Acute bolus injection of AAV vector (10^11-10^13 vg/mL, 1-5 mL volume) via eShunt lumen into CSF space; eShunt drainage paused for 1-4h post-injection to allow vector distribution.
M2_aav_gene_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.problem_addressed: CNS genetic diseases requiring intrathecal AAV delivery: SMA (Zolgensma), Batten disease, AADC deficiency, giant axonal neuropathy, muscular dystrophy (CNS variant).
M2_aav_gene_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.plausible_physical_principle: AAV vectors FDA-approved (Luxturna 2017, Zolgensma 2019). Intrathecal AAV delivery well-studied (Nusinersen precedent for intrathecal ASO; AAV9 crosses ependyma and transduces parenchyma after intrathecal delivery). Volume 1-5mL, distribution via bulk CSF flow + diffusion.
M2_aav_gene_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.magnitude_estimate: Intrathecal AAV9 dose 10^13-10^14 vg; transduces brain/spinal cord parenchyma for 5-10 years (episomal persistence). Clinically consequential (Zolgensma changes SMA trajectory).
M2_aav_gene_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.physics_verdict: PASSES_PHYSICS — acute bolus injection feasible; eShunt lumen diameter 1mm accommodates 1-5mL injection in 30-120s.
M2_aav_gene_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.physiology_verdict: PASSES_PHYSIOLOGY — intrathecal AAV delivery clinically established; pausing drainage for 1-4h post-injection does not cause ICP crisis in patient with otherwise patent eShunt (compensated hydrocephalus).
known_constraints: AAV9 capsid crosses ependyma but transduction is mostly periventricular; deeper structures limited
Pre-existing immunity to AAV9 (30-70% adult seroprevalence) limits re-dosing
Risk of dorsal root ganglia toxicity (FDA black box for Zolgensma intrathecal)
Volume 1-5mL exceeds eShunt lumen volume (~0.1mL) — injection is a BOLUS through the lumen, not a RESIDENT volume
M2_aav_gene_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.novelty_concern_pre_check: MEDIUM — Ommaya reservoir is standard-of-care for intrathecal delivery of AAV (NCT trials for SMA, Batten, AADC). Repeat Ommaya taps every 4-8 weeks are clinically routine. eShunt-specific value: (a) SINGLE permanent access (no reservoir replacement), (b) integrated with chronic drainage (patient needs drainage AND gene therapy), (c) targeted to specific CSF compartment (CP angle cistern vs ventricle vs lumbar).
M2_aav_gene_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.advance_verdict: CONDITIONALLY_NOVEL — survives physics; eShunt-specific value over Ommaya reservoir is INTEGRATION (chronic drainage + drug delivery in single device) and ANATOMICAL TARGETING (eShunt accesses CP angle cistern / subarachnoid compartment via venous route, distinct from ventricular Ommaya). Requires prior-art search.

M3_cell_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.core_mechanism: Acute bolus injection of stem cells / neural progenitors (10^6-10^7 cells/mL, 1-5 mL) via eShunt lumen into CSF; drainage paused 1-4h.
M3_cell_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.problem_addressed: ALS (NeurALT NCT), spinal cord injury, stroke recovery, neurodegenerative diseases, myelination disorders.
M3_cell_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.plausible_physical_principle: Intrathecal stem cell delivery established (StemCells Inc NCT trials; Neuralstem NCT trials). Cells migrate through CSF to injury site; cell diameter 10-20 μm passes through 1mm eShunt lumen easily.
M3_cell_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.magnitude_estimate: Intrathecal cell dose 10^7-10^8 cells; survival rate 1-10% engraftment; therapeutic effect window 3-12 months.
M3_cell_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.physics_verdict: PASSES_PHYSICS — but with two MATERIAL constraints.
known_constraints: ONE-WAY VALVE DAMAGE TO CELLS: eShunt's one-way valve (slit or ball-in-cone) imposes shear stress on cells passing through. Estimated shear 10-100 dyn/cm² — could damage cell membranes or trigger apoptosis. Cells would need to be injected on the CSF-side of the valve (distal port), bypassing valve passage.

LUMEN OCCLUSION BY AGGREGATES: 10^7 cells in 1mL = 10^7/mL concentration; cells aggregate in catheter, especially at bends; risk of lumen occlusion and shunt malfunction. Mitigated by anti-aggregation surfactants and slow infusion rate.
GRAFT-VERSUS-HOST if allogeneic; immunosuppression required
M3_cell_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.novelty_concern_pre_check: MEDIUM — intrathecal stem cell delivery established. eShunt-specific value: chronic access for repeated dosing (cell therapy often requires 3-6 monthly doses); access to specific CSF compartment.
M3_cell_therapy_via_eshunt_lumen.advance_verdict: CONDITIONALLY_NOVEL — survives physics but valve-damage and occlusion risks must be addressed in design (separate injection port distal to valve; slow infusion protocol). Lower priority than M2 (gene therapy is one-shot; cell therapy needs repeats).

M4_csf_sampling_diagnostic_port.core_mechanism: Percutaneous sampling port integrated into eShunt system allowing chronic CSF access for biomarker monitoring without repeat lumbar puncture.
M4_csf_sampling_diagnostic_port.problem_addressed: Chronic CSF biomarker monitoring for Alzheimer's (beta-amyloid, tau), tumor markers (cytology, AFP, hCG), infection detection (CSF culture, glucose, lactate).
M4_csf_sampling_diagnostic_port.plausible_physical_principle: Ommaya reservoir (1963 invention) is standard-of-care for chronic CSF sampling — silicone dome with self-sealing septum, percutaneous needle access. Volume 1-5 mL per sample.
M4_csf_sampling_diagnostic_port.magnitude_estimate: Sampling frequency: weekly-monthly for tumor monitoring; daily-weekly for infection; quarterly for Alzheimer's biomarkers.
M4_csf_sampling_diagnostic_port.physiology_verdict: PASSES_PHYSIOLOGY — chronic CSF access clinically established.
M4_csf_sampling_diagnostic_port.novelty_concern_pre_check: HIGHLY SATURATED — Ommaya reservoir is the textbook standard-of-care since 1963. ~60 years of clinical use; thousands of citations. eShunt-specific value would need to be: (a) integration with drainage (saves separate device), (b) anatomical targeting (CP angle cistern vs ventricle), (c) wireless sampling (no needle).
M4_csf_sampling_diagnostic_port.advance_verdict: SATURATED_FOR_PERCUTANEOUS_SAMPLING / CONDITIONALLY_NOVEL_FOR_WIRELESS_SAMPLING — basic sampling port is saturated; wireless sampling (microfluidic biosensor + RF readout) is novel but overlaps with M10 (biosensor integration).

M5_neuromodulation_electrode_via_venous_.core_mechanism: DBS electrode threaded through eShunt lumen into CSF space, providing deep brain stimulation via venous access route.
M5_neuromodulation_electrode_via_venous_.problem_addressed: Parkinson's, essential tremor, OCD, epilepsy — currently treated with DBS via cranial burr hole.
M5_neuromodulation_electrode_via_venous_.plausible_physical_principle: DBS electrodes (Medtronic, Boston Scientific, Abbott) are 1.27mm diameter quadripolar leads. Targets: STN (subthalamic nucleus), GPi (globus pallidus internus), VIM thalamus. All are DEEP PARENCHYMAL structures.
M5_neuromodulation_electrode_via_venous_.magnitude_estimate: DBS amplitude 1-3.5V, frequency 130-185Hz, pulse width 60-450μs. Clinically established efficacy.
M5_neuromodulation_electrode_via_venous_.physics_verdict: KILLED_BY_PHYSICS — DBS targets are anatomically INACCESSIBLE from the CSF space via venous route. STN is 8-12mm deep to the cortical surface, embedded in parenchyma; GPi is 12-18mm deep; VIM thalamus is 15-25mm deep. The eShunt accesses SUBARACHNOID space (between arachnoid and pia) — reaching deep nuclei would require parenchymal penetration, defeating the venous-access value proposition.
M5_neuromodulation_electrode_via_venous_.physiology_verdict: FAILED_PHYSIOLOGY — subarachnoid space does not provide electrical access to deep brain nuclei. Cortical surface stimulation (subdural electrodes) is a different therapy (neuroPace RNS for epilepsy) and uses different targets.
known_constraints: STN/GPi/VIM thalamus are DEEP PARENCHYMAL — not accessible from subarachnoid space
Electrical stimulation of subarachnoid space would stimulate cortical surface (causing seizures) not deep structures

Even if electrode penetrated parenchyma from subarachnoid space, trajectory would be cortical → white matter → deep nuclei — same burr-hole trajectory as standard DBS, no anatomical advantage from venous route
M5_neuromodulation_electrode_via_venous_.novelty_concern_pre_check: N/A — killed by physics before novelty assessment.
M5_neuromodulation_electrode_via_venous_.advance_verdict: KILLED_BY_PHYSICS — DBS targets anatomically inaccessible from eShunt's CSF-space access. PRESERVED AS HONEST NEGATIVE per #7 M10 lesson. Could potentially do CORTICAL surface stimulation (similar to neuroPace RNS subdural electrodes) but that is a different therapy with different indications (epilepsy, not movement disorders).
M5_neuromodulation_electrode_via_venous_.honest_negative_finding: eShunt's access to subarachnoid CSF space does NOT provide access to deep parenchymal structures. Neuromodulation of deep brain nuclei requires parenchymal electrode placement via cranial burr hole — the venous-access value proposition does not extend to deep brain stimulation. This is a fundamental anatomical constraint.

M6_car_t_immunotherapy_for_cns_tumors.core_mechanism: Acute bolus injection of CAR-T cells (targeting HER2, EGFRvIII, IL13Rα2, B7-H3) via eShunt lumen into CSF for treatment of leptomeningeal metastases / primary CNS tumors; drainage paused 1-4h post-injection.
M6_car_t_immunotherapy_for_cns_tumors.problem_addressed: Leptomeningeal metastases (5-8% of cancer patients, 1.5% lifetime risk in breast/lung/melanoma); primary CNS lymphoma; glioblastoma; medulloblastoma leptomeningeal spread.
M6_car_t_immunotherapy_for_cns_tumors.plausible_physical_principle: Intrathecal CAR-T NCT trials ongoing (Brescia 2024 published in Nature Medicine — complete response in leptomeningeal disease; City of Hope IL13Rα2 CAR-T NCT). Volume 1-5mL of CAR-T cell suspension (10^7-10^8 cells).
M6_car_t_immunotherapy_for_cns_tumors.magnitude_estimate: Leptomeningeal disease survival: 2-4 months untreated, 6-12 months with intrathecal CAR-T (early trial data). Clinically consequential.
M6_car_t_immunotherapy_for_cns_tumors.physics_verdict: PASSES_PHYSICS — same as M3 (cell therapy) but with additional considerations.
known_constraints: Same valve-damage risk as M3 (CAR-T cells must be injected DISTAL to one-way valve)
CAR-T cell exhaustion in CSF (low antigen density initially)
Cytokine release syndrome localized to CSF (neurotoxicity risk)
Requires repeated dosing (3-6 weekly intrathecal injections in trials)
M6_car_t_immunotherapy_for_cns_tumors.novelty_concern_pre_check: MEDIUM-HIGH — intrathecal CAR-T NCT trials use Ommaya reservoir or repeat LP. eShunt-specific value: (a) chronic access for REPEATED dosing (CAR-T requires 3-6 doses), (b) integration with drainage (leptomeningeal disease often causes hydrocephalus requiring shunting), (c) potential for continuous low-rate infusion (vs bolus).
M6_car_t_immunotherapy_for_cns_tumors.advance_verdict: CONDITIONALLY_NOVEL — survives physics; eShunt-specific value over Ommaya reservoir is REPEATED-DOSE convenience (CAR-T requires weekly intrathecal injections × 3-6 weeks) AND integration with drainage for hydrocephalus caused by leptomeningeal disease. Patient population NEEDS BOTH drainage AND drug delivery.

M7_anti_amyloid_antibody_via_eshunt.core_mechanism: Chronic access port via eShunt for repeated intrathecal delivery of anti-amyloid antibodies (aducanumab, lecanemab, gantenerumab) — bypassing BBB and reducing required dose 10-100x.
M7_anti_amyloid_antibody_via_eshunt.problem_addressed: Alzheimer's disease (50M globally; 10% of >65yr). IV anti-amyloid antibodies have ~0.1% BBB penetration; intrathecal delivery achieves 100-1000x higher CNS concentration at 1/10 the systemic dose.
M7_anti_amyloid_antibody_via_eshunt.plausible_physical_principle: Intrathecal anti-amyloid antibodies in clinical trials (gantenerumab intrathecal NCT; aducanumab intrathecal planned). Dose 10-100mg intrathecal vs 700mg IV (10 mg/kg × 70kg).
M7_anti_amyloid_antibody_via_eshunt.magnitude_estimate: Amyloid PET reduction with IV lecanemab: 60% centiloid reduction over 18 months. Intrathecal dosing could achieve higher CNS concentration with less ARIA (amyloid-related imaging abnormalities) risk.
M7_anti_amyloid_antibody_via_eshunt.physics_verdict: PASSES_PHYSICS for chronic access port — repeated bolus injections via eShunt-accessible port.
M7_anti_amyloid_antibody_via_eshunt.physiology_verdict: PASSES_PHYSIOLOGY — chronic access for monthly antibody injections is feasible.
known_constraints: BBB penetration of IV antibodies ~0.1%; intrathecal bypass achieves 100-1000x higher CNS level
ARIA risk (amyloid-related imaging abnormalities — edema/microhemorrhage) is dose-dependent; intrathecal lower systemic dose may REDUCE ARIA
Monthly injections × 18 months = 18 doses; eShunt-access port eliminates 18 repeat LPs
Alzheimer's patient population overlaps with NPH (often misdiagnosed) — some eShunt patients may benefit from concurrent anti-amyloid therapy
M7_anti_amyloid_antibody_via_eshunt.novelty_concern_pre_check: MEDIUM — intrathecal anti-amyloid trials exist (gantenerumab). eShunt-specific value: chronic access without repeat LP, integrated with drainage for NPH/Alzheimer's overlap population. Question: does intrathecal anti-amyloid + drainage integration represent a SYSTEM-LEVEL invention?
M7_anti_amyloid_antibody_via_eshunt.advance_verdict: CONDITIONALLY_NOVEL — survives physics; novel as a SYSTEM (chronic access + drainage + intrathecal delivery). Patient population overlap (NPH + Alzheimer's) is a unique angle. Lower priority than M2/M6 because IV anti-amyloid antibodies already FDA-approved (lecanemab 2023) — the value proposition is REDUCED DOSE / REDUCED ARIA, not access to therapy per se.

M8_chemotherapy_for_leptomeningeal_metas.core_mechanism: Acute bolus injection of chemotherapeutics (methotrexate, cytarabine, rituximab, trastuzumab) via eShunt lumen into CSF; drainage paused 1-4h post-injection for drug distribution.
M8_chemotherapy_for_leptomeningeal_metas.problem_addressed: Leptomeningeal metastases from breast, lung, melanoma; primary CNS lymphoma. Standard-of-care is intrathecal chemo via Ommaya reservoir (weekly methotrexate 10-15mg).
M8_chemotherapy_for_leptomeningeal_metas.plausible_physical_principle: Intrathecal chemo standard since 1970s. Drug distributes through CSF in 1-4h; pausing drainage extends dwell time.
M8_chemotherapy_for_leptomeningeal_metas.magnitude_estimate: Leptomeningeal disease median survival untreated 2-4 months; with intrathecal chemo 6-12 months. Clinically consequential.
M8_chemotherapy_for_leptomeningeal_metas.physics_verdict: PARTIAL_CONCERN — feasible for ACUTE bolus with drainage pause, BUT drainage pause is CONTRAINDICATED in patients with active hydrocephalus (high ICP at risk of herniation).
M8_chemotherapy_for_leptomeningeal_metas.physiology_verdict: FAILED_PHYSIOLOGY_FOR_HYDROCEPHALUS_POPULATION — eShunt patients have hydrocephalus or IIH requiring drainage; pausing drainage for 1-4h post-chemo risks ICP crisis. ONLY safe in compensated patients with low ICP.
known_constraints: Standard practice: Ommaya reservoir + ventricular drainage catheter on separate circuit (drainage continues during chemo dwell)
eShunt integrates drainage + delivery in ONE lumen — cannot drain AND dwell chemo simultaneously
For IIH patients (lower herniation risk): drainage pause for 1-4h may be acceptable
For obstructive hydrocephalus patients (higher herniation risk): drainage pause CONTRAINDICATED
DESIGN SOLUTION: dual-lumen eShunt (one lumen drains, second lumen delivers chemo) — but adds manufacturing complexity
M8_chemotherapy_for_leptomeningeal_metas.novelty_concern_pre_check: MEDIUM — Ommaya + EVD combination standard-of-care. eShunt-specific value: single integrated device (vs Ommaya + separate EVD). But this requires DUAL-LUMEN architecture which is novel engineering but adds risk.
M8_chemotherapy_for_leptomeningeal_metas.advance_verdict: PARTIAL_CONCERN — fails physiology for hydrocephalus population (drainage pause contraindicated). Survives only with dual-lumen architecture, which adds complexity. Lower priority than M2/M6 (which don't require drainage pause — cells/vector distribute and persist).

M9_continuous_icp_monitoring_standalone.core_mechanism: Wireless ICP sensor integrated into eShunt, providing continuous ICP monitoring as standalone diagnostic separate from drainage function.
M9_continuous_icp_monitoring_standalone.problem_addressed: Continuous ICP monitoring for trauma, post-SAH, IIH management. Current standard: invasive intraparenchymal bolt (Camino, Codman) or external ventricular drain.
M9_continuous_icp_monitoring_standalone.plausible_physical_principle: Wireless implantable pressure sensors established (CardioMEMS for HF; Neurovent P-Tel for ICP). eShunt already in CSF space — adding pressure sensor at distal tip is straightforward.
M9_continuous_icp_monitoring_standalone.magnitude_estimate: ICP range 0-50 mmHg, accuracy ±2 mmHg. Clinically established threshold.
M9_continuous_icp_monitoring_standalone.physiology_verdict: PASSES_PHYSIOLOGY — continuous ICP monitoring clinically valuable.
M9_continuous_icp_monitoring_standalone.novelty_concern_pre_check: ALREADY_COVERED — CereVasc has filed CEREVASC_INVENTION_002_V1 (Position 2 of 10) on 'Continuous, in-vivo, endogenous pressure-differential-based patency monitoring' with dual pressure sensors. The basic ICP-monitoring-on-eShunt concept is already in CereVasc's IP portfolio.
M9_continuous_icp_monitoring_standalone.advance_verdict: ALREADY_COVERED_BY_CEREVASC_POSITION_002 — duplicate of existing IP. Honest negative: this is not a NEW invention; it is Position 2.

M10_csf_biosensor_integration.core_mechanism: Wireless biosensor integrated into eShunt, continuously measuring CSF biomarkers (glucose, lactate, beta-amyloid, tau, alpha-synuclein, NfL, CRP, cytokines) and transmitting data externally.
M10_csf_biosensor_integration.problem_addressed: Chronic CSF biomarker monitoring for: (a) neurodegenerative disease progression (Alzheimer's beta-amyloid/tau; Parkinson's alpha-synuclein), (b) tumor markers (cytology, AFP, hCG for leptomeningeal disease), (c) infection detection (CSF glucose, lactate, WBC, CRP — early shunt infection), (d) metabolic monitoring (glucose, lactate for brain metabolism).
M10_csf_biosensor_integration.plausible_physical_principle: Implantable biosensors established (CGM for glucose since 1999; Eversense 90-day implantable CGM FDA-approved 2018). Electrochemical (amperometric, potentiometric), optical (fluorescence, Raman), and microfluidic (lab-on-chip) approaches all feasible. Continuous measurement + wireless transmission.
M10_csf_biosensor_integration.magnitude_estimate: Glucose mM range (3-5 mM CSF); lactate 1-2 mM; beta-amyloid 200-500 pg/mL; tau 200-500 pg/mL; NfL 10-1000 pg/mL. All within detection limits of current biosensors (detection limits pM-fM).
M10_csf_biosensor_integration.physics_verdict: PASSES_PHYSICS — sensor MEASURES rather than DELIVERS, so eShunt drainage does NOT compromise measurement. Sensor reads CSF continuously; drainage removes sampled CSF but sensor stays in place measuring new CSF as it flows past. UNIQUE PROPERTY: eShunt's drainage function is COMPATIBLE with continuous biosensing — unlike drug delivery which is compromised by drainage.
M10_csf_biosensor_integration.physiology_verdict: PASSES_PHYSIOLOGY — CSF biomarkers clinically validated; eShunt's CSF access is the natural sampling location.
known_constraints: Sensor drift: CGM drift ~5% over 14 days; CSF biosensor drift likely similar — chronic use requires recalibration protocol
Biofouling: protein adsorption on sensor surface; mitigated by anti-fouling coatings (PEG, zwitterionic polymers, T7 — but T7 is in TERRITORY #7)
Biomarker specificity: CSF biomarker thresholds differ from plasma; clinical interpretation needs validation
Multi-analyte: most useful to measure MULTIPLE biomarkers simultaneously — requires sensor array (microfabrication challenge)
eShunt-specific: drainage flow past sensor could ENABLE continuous fresh-CSF sampling (flow replenishes analyte) — could actually be ADVANTAGE over static Ommaya reservoir sampling
M10_csf_biosensor_integration.novelty_concern_pre_check: MEDIUM-HIGH — CGM-style continuous glucose monitoring is established; CSF biosensors are in research literature (microdialysis, lab-on-chip). eShunt-specific novel angle: (a) FIRST integrated endovascular-CSF-access biosensor, (b) drainage FLOW PAST sensor could enable continuous sampling without depletion (unique advantage vs static Ommaya sampling), (c) multi-analyte array on shunt body.
M10_csf_biosensor_integration.advance_verdict: CONDITIONALLY_NOVEL — survives physics; novel as SYSTEM-LEVEL invention (wireless CSF biosensor integrated into endovascular shunt with flow-past sampling). eShunt's drainage function is COMPATIBLE with sensing (unlike drug delivery which is compromised by drainage). LEADING CANDIDATE.

physics_precheck_summary.leading_candidate_after_physics_precheck: M10 — CSF biosensor integration. PASSES physics, NOVEL system-level invention, eShunt drainage is COMPATIBLE with sensing (unique advantage over drug delivery candidates which are compromised by drainage). Strongest candidate.
physics_precheck_summary.strong_alternative_after_physics_prechec: M2 — AAV gene therapy via eShunt. PASSES physics, eShunt adds chronic access value for repeated dosing.
physics_precheck_summary.parallel_candidate_after_physics_prechec: M6 — CAR-T immunotherapy. PASSES physics, eShunt adds repeated-dose convenience for CAR-T (3-6 weekly intrathecal injections).
honest_negatives_documented: M1 drug depot — eShunt drainage clears CSF-lumen-released drug too rapidly (5 min vs 30 min half-life vs VP shunt). Antibiotic prophylaxis saturated by Bactiseal/ARES.
M5 neuromodulation electrode — DBS targets (STN/GPi/VIM thalamus) anatomically INACCESSIBLE from subarachnoid CSF space. Killed by physics before prior-art search.

M8 chemotherapy for leptomeningeal metastases — drainage pause for drug dwell is CONTRAINDICATED in hydrocephalus patients (herniation risk). Survives only with dual-lumen architecture (adds complexity).
M9 continuous ICP monitoring — ALREADY COVERED by CereVasc Position 002 (dual pressure sensor patent filed). Duplicate, not new invention.
M4 CSF sampling port — SATURATED by Ommaya reservoir (60 years standard-of-care). Only novel as wireless sampling variant (overlaps with M10).
physics_precheck_summary.key_physics_insight: The eShunt's primary DRAINAGE function creates a fundamental tension with drug delivery (drug is drained away with CSF). This tension does NOT affect SENSORS (sensor reads CSF; drainage removes sampled CSF but sensor stays). The most eShunt-compatible CNS therapy platform mechanism is therefore BIOSIGNAL SENSING (M10) rather than drug delivery. Drug delivery candidates (M2/M6/M7) survive only if delivered as ACUTE BOLUS with drainage pause, or if dual-lumen architecture separates drainage from delivery lumen. This is a CRITICAL PHYSICS-DRIVEN PRIORITIZATION, not a preference.

M10_csf_biosensor.strongest_alternative: M2 (AAV gene therapy via eShunt) — addresses different CNS therapy problem (genetic disease vs chronic biomarker monitoring).
M10_csf_biosensor.what_failure_can_kill_us: Sensor drift / biofouling over chronic implant (5+ year eShunt lifespan) could render readings unreliable. CGM took 20+ years to mature; CSF biosensor may face similar maturity timeline.
M10_csf_biosensor.why_worth_keeping: First integrated wireless CSF biosensor on endovascular shunt. System-level invention that no competitor has. Compatible with eShunt's drainage function (uniquely). 50M Alzheimer's patients globally.

M2_aav_gene_therapy_via_eshunt.strongest_alternative: M10 (CSF biosensor) — also leverages eShunt's chronic CSF access but with no drainage-tension problem.
M2_aav_gene_therapy_via_eshunt.what_failure_can_kill_us: AAV9 seroprevalence (30-70% adults) prevents re-dosing; Ommaya reservoir is established standard-of-care with strong clinical inertia.
M2_aav_gene_therapy_via_eshunt.why_worth_keeping: Chronic access for repeated AAV dosing (SMA, Batten, AADC deficiency require lifetime therapy). Patient population overlaps with shunted hydrocephalus.

M6_car_t_immunotherapy_for_cns_tumors.strongest_alternative: M2 (AAV) — broader indications, less complex manufacturing (vector vs cell therapy supply chain).
M6_car_t_immunotherapy_for_cns_tumors.what_failure_can_kill_us: CAR-T manufacturing complexity (requires leukapheresis, ex vivo expansion, cryopreservation); eShunt vs Ommaya differentiation weak if dosing is monthly rather than weekly.
M6_car_t_immunotherapy_for_cns_tumors.why_worth_keeping: Leptomeningeal disease patients NEED BOTH drainage (hydrocephalus from leptomeningeal spread) AND CAR-T — single integrated device is genuinely valuable.
